meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_196_packages.json, all reference===196 edges from torahData.js (none existed), and the full source text torah_196.txt. For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset and whether it is assigned to a package. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ, מִלְּשׁוֹן, נִקְרָא, אֶלָּא) were considered. All four proposed bechina edges are new — Torah #196 had zero pre-existing edges in torahData.js.

analysis_notes.note_on_zero_existing_edges: Torah #196 was not represented in torahData.js at all prior to this analysis. The four bechina edges proposed in torah_196_packages.json (under 'proposed_new_bechina_edges') are entirely new and should be added to the dataset.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: לַעֲמֹד עַצְמוֹ (to stand firm / insist on)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 2: 'אָסוּר לָאָדָם לַעֲמֹד עַצְמוֹ עַל שׁוּם דָּבָר'. This phrase is used as an explanatory gloss for 'להתעקש' — both mean 'to insist.' It is not a new bechina concept but a Hebrew synonym for the same idea (להתעקש בתפלתו) already captured in Package 1. Not a gap.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: God is mentioned as the address of prayer throughout the text, but the Rebbe does not draw a bechina equivalence between God and any other concept in this Torah. God appears as the grammatical subject/object of the teaching, not as a bechina node. No bechina edge warranted.

The phrase is not equated to another concept through bechina language. No edge warranted.

structural_observations.teaching_type: This is primarily an ethical-practical teaching (mussar / halacha) with one core bechina identification. The eitza content far outweighs the bechina content — the Rebbe instructs HOW to pray (eitza) and identifies WHAT forced prayer IS (bechina). Torah #196 is unusual in having no bechina chains — only isolated pairs or very short chains.
structural_observations.good_evil_mirror: The teaching embeds a classic Good/Evil mirror at the level of prayer itself: the same act (prayer/תפלה) can be either holy (Package 2: prayer as mercy-and-supplication) or sinful (Package 1: prayer as robbery/demand). The concept תפלה thus bridges both packages — as proper prayer it is Package 2; as demanded prayer (תפלת קבע) it becomes the dominant concept of Package 1. This dual orientation of prayer is the central structural insight of Torah #196.
structural_observations.note_on_absence_of_biblical_character_no: Unlike most Likutay Moharan teachings, Torah #196 contains no symbolic figures (no patriarchs, kings, prophets, kabbalistic personae). The teaching is entirely abstract-ethical, operating only through the concepts of prayer, robbery, mercy, and supplication. This explains the minimal bechina content.
structural_observations.completeness_verdict: The two packages and four proposed bechina edges fully account for all bechina-identifiable concepts in Torah #196. No meaningful bechina gap was found.
